assumptions: Cases use synthetic article text in ordinary project files; no producer run, prior approval, external post, or provider connection is required.

When article_path is omitted, Tin uses a candidate only when exactly one article matches. Multiple files require an explicit path or caller-supplied article_text; Tin does not infer recency from filenames.

The optional writing-style guide is read from the current pinned project revision. Offline fixtures verify source selection and guards; live quality and cost remain unqualified until authorized evaluation.
cost_drivers: One gpt-6-sol call, at most 32000 serialized input bytes and 4096 output tokens. Full article and optional current style guide drive input size; overlong content fails before the call.
effects: Writes reports/SOCIAL_POST_BATCH.md in this project and enters normal human review. Tin never posts, schedules, or opens a pull request.

cases.description: One ordinary project article yields four grounded social drafts with exact source excerpts and no claim that the source was approved.
Caller-supplied article text can be used without a project article file.

inputs.article_text: A useful analytics chart begins with data that can be checked. The CSV import keeps each row tied to its original transaction. Teams can inspect an imported row and compare it with the source record before using the chart in a decision. The import records a validation result for each row and leaves invalid rows out of the chart.

rubric.question: Do all four draft claims follow from their cited excerpts and the full article, with no invented personal result, number, quotation or link?
Do the drafts fit the article's voice and, when present, the current writing-style guide without copying four near-identical hooks?
Can each post stand alone on its named platform and invite useful review without implying Tin posted or scheduled it?
